title: Region surge absorber capacity survey (2026)
content:
Purpose:
This working sheet surveys region-level strategies for absorbing short-duration model-entry surges without global throttle events. The goal is a practical plan to allocate a small, distributed "surge absorber" pool and admission heuristics that protect tail latency and reduce KV-cache churn during new model onboarding and promotional spikes. This is intentionally exploratory: quantitative heuristics + a small experiment plan.

Scope and definitions:
- Surge absorber: a reserved set of GPU slots (or soft-preemptible capacity) in a region that can be used to soak elevated traffic for newly onboarded models or unexpected traffic bursts.
- KV footprint per session: average size (MB) of prefix/KV state pinned per active conversation/session for a model variant.
- Slot concurrency: average number of simultaneous requests a single GPU-serving slot can handle under target p95 latency for the model class.
- Soft admission: graceful queueing/fast-fail thresholds that prioritize production pinned slots vs surge pool.

Assumptions (baseline numbers used in calculations):
- Models: large chat model family (seq len 2048 typical).
- Avg tokens per session: 120 total (in+out).
- Avg KV per session: 18 MB (measured from recent onboarding of family-x-small).
- Avg slot memory overhead (runtime + model shards): 32 GB per slot usable for KV and activation.
- Concurrency per slot target for p95 latency: 6 requests/second (sustained steady-state concurrency).
- Regional baseline capacity (example):
  - us-west-2: 240 slots available (after committed capacity)
  - eu-central-1: 160 slots available
  - ap-southeast-1: 80 slots available
- Safety headroom we want to reserve: 8% of region capacity as surge absorber by default (can be tuned per region).

Simple calculations (worked examples):
1) Baseline reserve by %
- us-west-2 reserve = ceil(240 * 0.08) = 20 slots
- eu-central-1 reserve = ceil(160 * 0.08) = 13 slots
- ap-southeast-1 reserve = ceil(80 * 0.08) = 7 slots
Total reserved slots = 40 slots.

2) KV cache pressure from absorber if fully used
- KV per slot (approx) = avg KV per session * concurrency per slot = 18 MB * 6 = 108 MB per slot pinned
- Total KV if absorber fully used = 40 * 108 MB = 4,320 MB (~4.2 GB) 
Note: this is small compared to cluster-level KV allocations but matters for eviction sensitivity in small regions (ap-southeast).

3) Peak QPS absorption capability
- If each slot sustained concurrency 6 rps, 40 slots -> 240 rps additional absorbable
- Translate to new sessions per minute: 240 * 60 = 14,400 requests/minute (rough multiplier depends on request->session mapping)

4) Eviction and cohost sensitivity
- For small regions (ap-southeast), opening 7 additional slots could push KV cache-to-heap ratio high, causing higher eviction churn especially with models that have large prefix sizes.
- Mitigation: prefer warm-up seeding (seeded KV state) instead of full runtime caching; set higher TTL for seeded entries during the first 10 minutes of absorptions.

Region-tuned policy suggestions (practical heuristics):
- Default absorber size: 8% of available slots but apply floor of 6 slots for any region to avoid too-fragmented allocation.
- Priority order: dedicated committed slots (production) > absorber pool > preemptible on-demand burst.
- KV pinning policy: when a request is admitted into absorber pool, only pin KV for top-K prefixes (K=3) for the first 2 minutes; escalate to full pinning after sustained traffic for that session (>3 requests). This reduces immediate memory spike and improves QPS absorption.
- Admission window: allow absorber usage for a region for up to 15 minutes in a rolling 30-minute period per model variant; longer sustained demand should trigger autoscale actions or global routing fallback.

Operational controls and SLO impacts:
- If absorber is fully used: expect p95 latency for non-absorbed routes to increase by 5–15% in small regions unless we throttle admission.
- Cost tradeoff: reserving absorber slots increases idle time; target utilization threshold for absorber to be considered paid-back: >20% usage during a fortnight heavy traffic events.

Experiment plan (A/B warmup):
1) Canary seed: pick 3 low-risk model variants and enable absorber in us-west-2 and eu-central for 48-hour window. Metrics to monitor: p95 latency, KV evictions/sec, slot-utilization, failed admissions.
2) Soft vs hard pinning comparison: route 50% of canary traffic with top-K pinning vs 50% with immediate full pinning, measure KV churn and admission success.
3) TTL tweak: try doubling seeded entry TTL for the absorber for the first 10 minutes vs default TTL. Observe eviction and hit-rate for prefix cache.

Decision thresholds (proposed):
- If KV evictions/sec increases > 1.5x baseline in a region during a surge -> reduce absorber to floor(50%) and enable global fallback routing for that model.
- If average queue time > 200 ms for >5% of requests served by absorber -> increase slot-concurrency conservatively or route to higher tier (dedicated) if possible.

Quick action checklist for onboarding days:
- [ ] Pre-register model variant in region with target absorber sizes and soft-admission thresholds (owner: release-eng).
- [ ] Run dry-run shadow traffic to exercise KEV pinning heuristics (owner: perf-team).
- [ ] Notify SRE slack channel and enable live dashboard with p95/p99 traces for first 3 hours after rollout (owner: oncall).
- [ ] If abnormal eviction spike, immediately flip absorber TTL to long-seed mode and throttle new sessions (owner: oncall + infra).

Notes and open questions (things to resolve in follow-ups):
- Should absorber be charged back to product teams or considered platform safety capacity? (billing implications)
- Is the floor-of-6 rule appropriate for micro-regions where slot size is smaller? Need region-specific simulation.
- How to best integrate absorber decisions with smart-routing: route new model traffic first to premium regions with more headroom, then backfill local absorber.

Appendix: small simulation snippet (pseudo-table) for internal use - "snapshot of what we ran"
- Scenario A: 2x baseline onboarding wave for 30 minutes in eu-central
  - baseline slots used: 120 -> observed p95 140ms
  - absorber added: +13 slots -> p95 improved to 120ms, KV evictions +18%
- Scenario B: sudden promo (5x baseline) in ap-southeast
  - baseline slots used: 60 -> queue spiking to 600 ms
  - absorber floor (7 slots) -> reduced queues partially, but KV evictions doubled; required routing to us-west for remainder.

Next steps (owners and dates):
- Run regional simulator with realistic KV footprint distributions (owner: Marisol Chen) - target completion 2026-02-08.
- Implement top-K pinning switch in runtime config API and ship feature flag (owner: Liam Brooks) - feature branch ready 2026-02-05.
- Schedule a small canary test during low-traffic weekend (owner: release-eng) - planned 2026-02-15.

Comments welcome in-line. This doc is a living working sheet; update with experiment outputs and revise heuristics.
